text: {"hypotheses":[{"statement":"The accuracy drop observed in the naive‑append baseline of the ICLR rewrite‑vs‑append ablation is caused by cross‑fact interference that grows with store size, as documented in the consolidation literature; therefore, inserting a periodic consolidation step that compresses the accumulated store into a summary should restore QA accuracy to near‑rewrite levels.","confidence":0.78,"support_ids":["e8a6939f","98edf81f"],"tags":["interference","consolidation","ablation","memory"]},{"statement":"Applying MemGPT’s virtual context paging mechanism to the append baseline will offload older or less relevant items to external memory, preventing token‑budget overflow by day 20 while preserving performance, effectively combining paging with the rewrite strategy for scalable memory management.","confidence":0.65,"support_ids":["e8a6939f","df71618a","4779d87a"],"tags":["MemGPT","paging","token_budget","rewrite","scalability"]}]}
